items.title: Reading 4 · Unit 1
items.scene: A school proposes replacing a small garden with a theatre. Supporters say the theatre would allow more students to perform. Opponents value the garden as a quiet place. A survey records how often both spaces would be used, but it does not measure how strongly students value them. The committee postpones its decision.
items.prompt: What limitation of the survey is described?
items.answer: Frequency of use does not measure the strength of students’ preferences.
options: Frequency of use does not measure the strength of students’ preferences.
It proves that everyone wants a theatre.
It contains no information about use.
It shows that the garden is unused.
items.why: The survey measures frequency but leaves strength of preference unmeasured. It cannot answer both questions at once.
items.hint: Separate what the text says from what you can only guess.

items.title: Reading 4 · Unit 1
items.scene: A school proposes replacing a small garden with a theatre. Supporters say the theatre would allow more students to perform. Opponents value the garden as a quiet place. A survey records how often both spaces would be used, but it does not measure how strongly students value them. The committee postpones its decision.
items.prompt: What would best address that limitation?
items.answer: Ask students to explain why each space matters to them.
options: Ask students to explain why each space matters to them.
Repeat the same usage count only.
Remove the garden before consulting students.
items.why: Explanations can reveal why a space matters. Another count alone would repeat the same limitation.
items.hint: Separate what the text says from what you can only guess.
